fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Dense Vegetation; Access Drive; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Single Access Point; Limited Visibility
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive to allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Clear vegetation back from the walls and roofline of both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move around the buildings on foot.
• Cut back any branches overhanging the access drive that could block ladder trucks or other tall emergency vehicles.
• Mark the detached structure with a visible address or unit identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main residence on arrival.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials so the full width is available to emergency vehicles at all times.
• Thin dense vegetation between the two structures to give responders a clear path between them during operations.
• Post the property address on both ends of the access drive if it runs a significant distance from the road, so responders can confirm they are on the correct route.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Large Trees; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Near Structure; Single Access Route; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation; Mixed Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and low-growing plants that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Remove or cut back ground vegetation growing close to the base of the structure on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters near the house so individual trees are no longer touching or overlapping each other with their branches.
• Raise the lower branches of large trees near the house by trimming them up from the ground to create open space beneath them.
• Separate shrubs and ground plants from the base of large trees so vegetation is not connected from the ground up into the tree canopy.
• Clear ground vegetation and low shrubs along the sides and rear of the house where access is limited.
• Cut back or remove mixed shrubs and plants growing between the scattered trees and the structure.
• Keep the single driveway clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along its full length.
• Trim any branches hanging over the driveway that could block a fire truck from passing through.
• Clear a path wide enough for a person to walk completely around the rear of the structure.
• Remove dead or dry ground cover that has accumulated beneath trees and near the house.
• Thin scattered trees closest to the structure to create more open ground between them and the building.
